A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spider 2.0 benchmark and Spider-Agent study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original model and framework evaluations, including Spider 2.0 success rates, text-to-SQL execution accuracies, ablations, and error analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds Spider-Agent evaluations on Spider 2.0-lite and Spider 2.0-snow in Table 4.

M1.justification: The documented Spider-Agent interaction loop, action space, termination rules, and prompts remain unchanged in Appendix C. V2 mentions variants and evaluates additional models and settings, but does not document a changed algorithm or method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same reported benchmark coverage: 632 Spider 2.0 tasks and 547 tasks each for lite and snow, with unchanged database systems and task categories. Additional agent evaluations use these existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands comparisons on lite/snow by adding Spider-Agent evaluations alongside the retained DIN-SQL, DAIL-SQL, CHESS, and CodeS results. New evaluated models include o3-mini, DeepSeek-V3, and Qwen2.5-Coder. The original full Spider 2.0 framework comparison remains in Table 6.

E3.justification: V2 adds agent evaluations on lite/snow and removes the reference-plan control from Table 10. Section 4.2 also changes the stated scope of the 300-example error analysis from agents and text-to-SQL parsers to code agents. SR/EX definitions and difficulty thresholds remain unchanged; these edits do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The reference-plan ablation testing whether explicit solution plans improve SQL generation is removed from Section 4.3 and Table 10. Most other analyses remain: the dialect comparison and pass@n plot move to Appendix C.4, while few-shot, oracle-function, task-subset, and case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: No new seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported. The relocated pass@n plot retains the same reporting.

E6.justification: Reported full Spider 2.0 success rates change substantially: o1-preview moves from 17.01% to 21.36%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet from 9.02% to 14.87%, and GPT-4o from 10.13% to 12.34%. New Table 4 reports lite/snow results, including 23.40% for o3-mini on lite and 23.77% for o1-preview on snow. Full-benchmark difficulty breakdowns disappear, several subset scores change, and Table 10 relabels o1-preview's 12.60% reference-plan result as without oracle functions. Table 5 remains unchanged; the reasons for the revised scores are unspecified.

T1.justification: The formal task definitions in Section 2.1 and execution-based evaluation definitions in Appendix A, including Equations 1–2, are unchanged. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the enterprise workflow benchmark, its lite/snow settings, and Spider-Agent. Both versions conclude that existing models remain inadequate for these tasks. Updated headline percentages revise the supporting empirical results without changing the contribution's scope or central conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 removes the interpretation that reference plans help through step-by-step SQL construction, and drops the discussion linking diminishing pass@n gains to benchmark difficulty and annotation quality. The principal explanations involving schema linking, document grounding, SQL dialects, and project exploration remain.

D1.justification: Table 13 gains the previously blank rewritten gold-SQL example, improving annotation documentation without establishing a dataset change. Conversely, the retained pass@n experiment loses its explicit temperature-1.0 sampling description. Core prompts, action specifications, budgets, and resource-access information remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds DSBench by Jing et al. and removes the SPOC citation by Kulal et al. Detailed descriptions of earlier text-to-SQL datasets are compressed into a collective citation, while the positioning around realistic enterprise workflows remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 revises the results narrative, reorders task-type analyses, introduces Appendix C.4 for relocated discussion, and condenses related work. It also updates the conference header and acknowledgements. These are localized revisions within the retained overall structure.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized: a new lite/snow results table becomes Table 4, the original full-benchmark table becomes a compact overall-only Table 6, and Table 10 loses its reference-plan column. The pass@n plot and dialect table move to the appendix, Table 13 gains its missing SQL panel, and success-case figures are regrouped.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens useful model comparisons and repairs Table 13's missing example, but removes a useful planning ablation and leaves important reporting discrepancies unexplained. Table 10 now shows o1-preview scoring 12.60% without oracle functions versus 9.51% with them, contrary to the retained general benefit claim. Appendix Table 20 also retains 17.0% overall success alongside 21.36% in Table 6. These unresolved issues prevent a reliable judgment that the added evidence produces a net quality improvement.
